# Word bank — woodworking

Modifier taxonomy is in core `format-bank-master.md` §5–§6; this file holds the woodworking phrases and vocabulary. Persona locks apply: Dale and Hank (the for-profit channels) get the full bank plus §7; Kenji and Sam exclude big-box, disposable, speed and money-in anchors.

## 1. Caps-worthy power words (niche-proven)

NEVER · STOP · SECRET(S) · GENIUS · THOUSANDS · FREE · GUARANTEED · FOREVER · ANY · ALL · EVERY · FATAL · BANNED · REAL · TRUTH · ACTUALLY · WRONG · PRO(S) · MASTER · AMAZING · PERFECT · FLAWLESS · EXPENSIVE · WORTH IT. Use 1–3 per title.

## 2. Modifier phrases by family

- **Parentheticals** — objection-killer: "(No Special Tools)", "(No Table Saw)", "(No Experience Needed)". Adversary tag: "(Woodworking Stores Hate This)", "(The Pros Never Mention It)". Credibility tag: "(Beginner's Guide)", "(40 Years of Pro Tips!)", "(The Japanese Way)". Surprise tease: "(The Results Will SURPRISE You!)". Insider-term / loophole: "(The Particleboard Lie)", "(The Supply-Grade Secret)". Guilt hook: "(You're Probably Doing It)", "(You're Wasting a Goldmine)". Value verdict: "(Worth It!)", "(And 5 to Skip)", "(Total Waste of Money)".
- **Urgency:** Before Your Next Project · This Weekend · Right Now · Before You Buy Anything Else · Before Winter.
- **Totality / whole-shop:** Every Project · EVERY Cut · Completely · ALL.
- **Permanence / certainty:** FOREVER · PERMANENTLY · GUARANTEED · Never Again · Lasts Generations.
- **Effort negation (stackable, staccato proven):** No Table Saw · No Power Tools · No Fancy Jigs · No Experience · No Mess. "No Nails. No Glue."
- **Named-retailer / lumber anchor (Dale only):** "Using Only Wood From Lowe's" · "One $5 Board From Home Depot".
- **Money-loss present tense:** "That's Costing You Money" · "Is Ruining Your Furniture" · "You're Wasting".
- **Sells / value framing:** "That SELL for Stupid Money" · "That Look Like You Spent THOUSANDS" — both proven on scrap topics. For the full for-profit vocabulary see §7.
- **Ironic-burden / twist parenthetical (for-profit, proven in the ecosystem — core §5):** "(Unfortunately)" · "(almost)" · "— and It's KILLING Me" · "I Almost Kept It Myself". Objection-killer for the tool-cost doubt: "(Even After Buying ALL the Tools)" ← "I buy ALL the tools to build it, and still profit $100." · 956k.
- **Title-thumbnail interlock:** "Stop Building Birdhouses Like THIS" (161k) — proven in the pool.

## 3. Register vocabularies

- **Lost-wisdom (Sam's native register):** old-school · old-timers · before power tools · the way it's always been done · still unbeaten · grandpa's · swore by · generations · the joint furniture makers used for 200 years.
- **Precision / mastery (Kenji):** razor-sharp · dead-flat · no nails · no glue · hairline · the Japanese way · the secret the West never learned · mirror finish · the one joint · the sharpening secret.
- **Friendly-thrifty (Dale, pre-pivot general lane — parked):** cheap · scrap · one board · $5 · beginner · stop wasting · actually need.
- **Hustle-thrifty / money-in (Dale post-pivot and Hank):** sells · sells out · sold out · orders · buyers · profit · margin · "for $X" · "cost me $X" · side hustle · craft fair · Etsy · Marketplace · "40 years of selling" (Dale only) · "I can't make these fast enough" · "here's how" · "how I".

## 4. Exclusivity ladder (climb as needed)

Most beginners get this wrong → Pros don't talk about it → Nobody teaches → NO ONE knows about → The industry pretends it doesn't exist.

## 5. Niche vocabulary

- **Sensory / quality symptoms (title in the viewer's words):** blotchy · tearout · wobbly · gappy · split · warped · dull · racking · ugly gaps · won't close · rubbing.
- **Material / behavior protagonists:** sawdust · offcuts · scrap · a single 2x4 · one board — proven to carry a title on their own. **Added 2026-09-09 (for-profit intake):** pallets / palletwood (Use PALLETWOOD to make MONEY and learn woodworking. · 2.6M; 100+ Pallet Projects To Start a Small Business For Beginners · 750k), scrap 2x6, "scrap wood you already have", sawdust-as-product (Everyone Throws Sawdust Away...Here's How to SELL IT! · 1.7M), fence pickets (killed on the own channels), twigs (killed), cardboard.
- **Adversary roster:** big-box furniture makers · tool marketers · "the woodworking stores" · brand manufacturers · the disposable-furniture industry. **For-profit additions:** "Big Box" as the parenthetical adversary ("(Big Box Hates Me)", "(Big Box HATES This)" — both operator-selected 2026-09-09), stores that throw out pallets, boutiques charging $475, "people who think it's hard".

## 6. Candidates (unproven finds — test per core `filing-rule.md` §3)

- **Caps candidates from the operator's greenlit for-profit titles (2026-09-09; candidate until views):** INSANE · RIDICULOUS · DESPERATE · STUPID (Easy) · SERIOUS (Money) · FASTER · SELL OUT / SOLD OUT · IMPOSSIBLE (to Sell) · DOUBLE · NOTHING (Cost Me NOTHING) · EVERYTHING · ILLEGAL (single quotes, per house style).

- "Holy Grail of X" (trim ecosystem, 7M / 6y) — dated packaging on a durable topic; candidate as a phrase only.
- "That Changes Everything!!!" (trim ecosystem, 2.6M / 2y) — candidate terminus.
- "Literally Defy Gravity" — produced on the illusion sub-angle, no data yet.

## 7. For-profit vocabulary (Dale post-pivot and Hank; register-locked off Kenji and Sam)

Sources are the for-profit intake (observed 2026-06-22; raw set in `archive/hank-hardwood-intake-2026-06.md`) and the operator's own greenlit titles. Modifier taxonomy — the earned-income scale and the ironic-burden parenthetical — lives in core `format-bank-master.md` §5.

- **Demand-overload phrases (F51):** I CAN'T Make These Fast Enough · Sell FASTER Than You Can Build Them · NON-STOP Orders · So Many Orders · I Literally SOLD OUT · Sells Out the SAME DAY · SELL OUT Every Single Time · They ALL Sold · Buyers Are FIGHTING Over · Can't Keep Them in Stock · I Can't Stop Selling · sell like Hotcakes · hot selling · consistently sells everywhere I go · Never Once Came Home With Me.
- **Money-in phrases (the earned-income scale):** Make Money Woodworking (series suffix) · Low Cost High Profit (modular prefix) · Huge Profit · High Profit · Maximum Profit · Make A Fortune · Prints Money · MONEY MAKER · Side Hustle · $X/Month · 650% Profit · Highest-Margin · Minimal Materials, Maximum Profit · Smalls That Sell · Easy to Make. Easier to Sell. · Start a Small Business · Replace Your Entire Salary / Replaced My Full-Time Income · THOUSANDS in Pure Profit · "bucks" (casual register: 100 bucks an hour, sells for 10 bucks).
- **Arbitrage phrases (F52):** They Sell These for $X — I Build Mine for $Y · They Want $X…You Can Build It For $Y · Costs $X to Build and Sells for $Y · $X in Wood, $Y in Sales · People Pay $X for This $Y Build · Charge DOUBLE · Made Me More Than … Did.
- **Free-material phrases:** FREE Pallet Wood · Free Pallets Build EVERYTHING I Sell · I Haven't Paid for Lumber in 10 Years · Cost Me NOTHING to Make · Everyone THROWS AWAY · Stores THROW OUT · You're Sitting on FREE Wood · Scrap Wood You Already Have.
- **CTA tails (operator-endorsed 2026-06-22):** Try This TODAY · Start TODAY · Do This Now · Build One TODAY · Pick One, Start TODAY · … Here's How.
- **Tenure money-keys (Dale's wording; Hank may claim tenure in his own words, operator 2026-10-20):** In 40 Years, [X] Is the Most Profitable Thing I've Ever Sold · 40 Years of Selling · The $10 Flip I've Done for 40 Years · 40 Years Later · I've Used for 40 Years.
- **Series-brand convention (candidate):** the Matthew Peech module stack `[The $X Product] - Low Cost High Profit - Make Money Woodworking (Episode N)` (3.1M ceiling on "Low Cost High Profit - Small Projects That Sell - Make Money Woodworking (Episode 2)") and the serialized listicle `[N] More … That Sell - [Wedding / Fall] Edition` (376k / 316k). Candidate for an own series brand; not yet used.
- **Style locks from the operator's edits:** CAPS on the single highest-emotion word; drop "no one knows" where a listicle count already carries the title; parentheticals for the twist only — demand proof spelled out as a clause; "How I…" and "…Here's How" native on both for-profit channels; both may use "I" (Hank need not always be first person).
- **Two title philosophies (both earn views):** hook-driven (the own channels, browse) and SEO-stacked (keyword-dense — "Wooden craft ideas and scrap wood projects ideas to make money fast as a woodworker" · 1.0M / 3y).
